title: Pretorius Blasts 66 off 26 Balls as San Francisco Unicorns Demolish Washington Freedom by Eight Wickets to Go Top of the MLC Table
excerpt: Lhuan-dre Pretorius smashed seven sixes and Finn Allen added a blistering 45 off 18 as the Unicorns chased down 191 in just 15.1 overs in Grand Prairie — the most dominant chase of the MLC 2026 season so far
body:
The San Francisco Unicorns made a statement in Grand Prairie on Sunday night, mauling Washington Freedom's total of 190/4 with nearly five overs to spare to claim an emphatic eight-wicket victory. The win lifts them to the top of the MLC 2026 standings.

Lhuan-dre Pretorius, the 22-year-old South African wicketkeeper-batsman who has been the breakout star of this MLC season, set the tone from the very first over. He crashed seven sixes and three fours on his way to 66 off just 26 balls — a strike rate of 253.85 that left Freedom's attack in ruins before the powerplay was over.

At the other end, New Zealand's Finn Allen played the role of chief enabler, hammering 45 off 18 deliveries with four fours and four sixes of his own, at a strike rate of 250. The pair's opening assault ensured the required rate never climbed above a run a ball, turning what should have been a tense chase into a procession.

## Hardie Finishes the Job in Style

When Pretorius and Allen finally departed, Australia's Aaron Hardie took over with clinical precision. The 26-year-old all-rounder peppered the boundary in the middle overs — smashing back-to-back fours off South Africa's Marco Jansen in the 13th over and earlier launching a six off New Zealand's Lockie Ferguson in the 11th. Hardie and captain Matt Short guided the Unicorns home without further alarm, reaching 193/2 in 15.1 overs.

The run rate of 12.73 through the chase was the highest in any completed second innings this MLC season, a testament to the Unicorns' fearless batting philosophy.



> **"## Hardie Finishes the Job in Style

When Pretorius and Allen finally departed, Australia's Aaron Hardie took over with clinical precision."**


## Freedom's Big Names Fall Flat

Washington Freedom, who won the toss and elected to bat, had posted a competitive 190/4 off their 20 overs — a total anchored by contributions from their international stars. But their bowling, which includes the likes of Ferguson (3-0-45-0), Jansen, and Nikhil Chaudhary (4-0-29-1), was simply overwhelmed by the ferocity of the Unicorns' hitting.


![Grand Prairie — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Grand_Prairie_May_2019_27_%28Market_Square_water_tower%29.jpg/3840px-Grand_Prairie_May_2019_27_%28Market_Square_water_tower%29.jpg)


Ferguson, one of the fastest bowlers in world cricket, conceded 45 runs in just three overs and went wicketless. Jansen, the towering South African left-armer, was carted for boundaries by Hardie in the 13th over. Chaudhary, who had been the hero of Freedom's previous match with a last-ball six against Texas Super Kings, was the only bowler to claim a wicket.

## Unicorns Take Pole Position

The victory — the Unicorns' third win in five matches — lifts them to the top of the MLC 2026 points table with six points, clear of the chasing pack. Seattle Orcas, Texas Super Kings, and Washington Freedom are all bunched on four points apiece.

San Francisco's campaign has been built on explosive batting. In their previous outing, Pretorius had hammered 87 off 39 balls in a thriller against the Seattle Orcas, while Brody Couch has proven a reliable presence lower down the order. With Pakistan's Haris Rauf and Australia's Xavier Bartlett leading the bowling attack, the Unicorns look the most balanced side in the competition.

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

MLC has rapidly become appointment viewing for the Indian diaspora in America. The league's six franchises — spread from New York to California — offer NRIs the chance to watch world-class T20 cricket live on US soil, often in their own backyards. Sunday's match in Grand Prairie, Texas drew a significant crowd of South Asian fans, many of whom had driven from Dallas, Houston, and beyond.

The Unicorns, based in the San Francisco Bay Area but playing their early-season games in Texas, have a particular pull among the tech-heavy Indian community in Silicon Valley. Their next home stretch will give Bay Area fans a chance to watch Pretorius, Allen, and company dismantle bowling attacks in person.

With the MLC season running through July 18, the business end of the tournament is approaching fast. The Unicorns sit pretty at the top — and on this form, they'll take some stopping.

**Brief scores:** Washington Freedom 190/4 (20 overs) lost to San Francisco Unicorns 193/2 (15.1 overs; Pretorius 66 off 26, Allen 45 off 18; Chaudhary 1-29) by 8 wickets.
